items.stem: Which use of AI best respects academic integrity?

options.text: Submitting AI-written answers as your own
options.rationale: Passing AI work off as your own breaches integrity.

options.text: Using AI to explain a concept you then learn and write yourself
options.rationale: Correct: AI supports understanding without replacing your work.

options.text: Having AI take an online test for you
Copying AI text verbatim into an essay
options.rationale: Verbatim copying without attribution breaches integrity.

items.explanation: Correct: using AI to explain a concept you then learn and express yourself respects integrity.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO habits make AI practice questions effective for learning? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Attempting each question before revealing the answer
Reading only the answers without attempting them
options.rationale: Reading answers alone gives weak recall.

options.text: Reviewing and re-attempting the questions you got wrong
Generating questions but never taking them
options.rationale: Unused questions do not help learning.

items.explanation: Correct: attempting before checking and reviewing mistakes both strengthen recall.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An AI tool gives a confident but unfamiliar historical date. What should you do first?

options.text: Verify the date against a trusted source before using it
options.rationale: Correct: AI confidence is not proof of accuracy.

options.text: Trust it because the tool sounded certain
Assume it is wrong and ignore it
options.rationale: Reflexively ignoring it is as unjustified as blind trust.

options.text: Ask the same tool to confirm itself

items.explanation: Correct: verify it against a trusted source, because confident AI answers can be wrong.
